cells.tense: You are here with the pen, at the end of a made thing, and this is being let go in time.
cells.act: accept the acknowledgment when it comes
cells.ask: When someone names what you carried, agree out loud once — no deflect, no downplay — and close the exchange there.
cells.core:
You can finish a thing and hand it on without holding it up. Something you carried for someone is nearly done, and letting go reads as the last part of the work rather than a loss. The release is running on the work itself, not on will, and it arrives while the thing is still warm.
Someone has started to notice what it took. When they say it, agree out loud once instead of waving it away — the finish needs a witness more than a speech, and receiving it is the whole move. The exchange ends when you let it end; the next thing starts clean because this one did.
cells.sheetLine: You can finish a thing and hand it over without a fight.
cells.verb: tending what is growing with care, in form
cells.place: the point where a made thing is finished and released

cells.tense: You are bracing at a completion that cannot be written in yet, pushing this ahead of its own timing.
cells.act: let the satisfaction of a finished thing land
cells.ask: Stay with one finished piece for a day — use it, look at it, eat off it — and don't open the next job in your head.
cells.core:
The next job is being solved before this one is done. You are at the end of work that is already good and you want to take it further; the taste of the finished piece has started to feel like a stop you can't afford. The real ending arrives after no one mentions it anymore, and that is the stretch the people close to you clock.
Stay with one finished piece for a day. Use it, look at it, eat off it — not the next improvement, the thing itself. Vision comes from what has been fully taken in, so the future you're bracing for gets clearer once the last piece has actually been sat with. The cost is one day of not improving anything; that is what keeps the next thing your own.
cells.sheetLine: You're building the next thing before this one is finished.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door already behind you, holding this back from its own completion.
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Take the half-finished piece and give it fifteen minutes this week — the same one, no new start, no verdict on the whole.
cells.core:
Something got far enough to be nearly over and you went on holding it long after it needed holding. The hours still go to the old round, the old ritual still gets done, and it is finished — you've kept it in the schedule as if it weren't. Anyone close can tell, and you've been calling that keeping up.
Take the half-finished piece and give it fifteen minutes this week. The same one, no new start, no verdict on the whole. Energy into what you already chose pulls the current through the starved part; the ending settles once you're moving again. You don't need a sign it will be worth it to take the next small step.
cells.sheetLine: It's finished. You've gone on tending it anyway.
cells.verb: tending what is growing with care, in form

cells.tense: You are at the end of the made thing, doing the last of the carrying now, and not signing it.
cells.act: make the sacrifice visible without explaining it
cells.ask: Next time you carry something for someone, do that part where they can see it, and say nothing about why.
cells.core:
The finish keeps happening and the one who finished it keeps going unnamed — and the unnamed one is you. You are at the end of something you made, doing the last part where it could be seen, and the story among the people is that it happened by itself or that somebody else arranged it. Nobody's asking. What you gave up is being authored and the author isn't signing.
Do the next part where they can see it. The piece you would normally do unseen — do that one in front of the person it's for, and say nothing about what it costs. The finished thing gets its edge back; it belongs to someone again. If they name it, receive that rather than deflecting.
cells.sheetLine: The carry is done, by you, and no one knows.
cells.verb: tending what is growing with care, in form
cells.place: the point where a made thing is finished and released
